1
Matam-e-Shabir Kar Ke Le Lo Zahra Ki Dua.
Sans Aye Ya Na Aye Zindagi Ka Kya Pata.
Rona Hai Apni Ibadat Yeh Bhala Kaise Ruke.
Keh Ke Matam Hum Karein Gay Haye Zainab Ki Rida.

2
Roye The Yaqub Apne Baite Yousuf Ke Liye.
Hum Kahein Jo Haye HUssaina Tum Ko Lagta Hai Bura.
Choda So Saloon Se Jari Matam-e-Shabir Hai.
Ta Hashar Ye Na Ruke Ga Ye Tha Zainab Ne Kaha.

3
Hath Hai Ik Seene Par Our Dosre Mein Hai Allam.
Yaad Kar Ke Ro Rahe Hain Maula Ghazi Ki Wafa.
Bint-e-Zahra Ki Dua Hai Gham Jo Likhta Hai Sajjad.
Razi Hoon Gi Pak Bibi Noha Asghar Wo Suna.

/bin/bash -lc "python - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
p = 'src/data/lyrics/matam-e-shabir-kar-ke-le-lo-zahra-ki-dua-tajpoints-7444f44eef1f205f80e8.md'
old = subprocess.check_output(['git', 'show', 'HEAD:' + p], text=True).split('---', 2)[2].strip()
_, header, body = Path(p).read_text().split('---', 2)
roman = '\\n'.join(line.removeprefix('  ') for line in header.split('romanLyrics: |-\\n', 1)[1].splitlines()).strip()
assert old.lower().replace('.\\n','\\n').removesuffix('.') == roman.lower()
for section, numbers in [(roman, '123'), (body, '۱۲۳')]:
    groups = [group.splitlines() for group in section.strip().split('\\n\\n')]
    assert [group[0] for group in groups] == list(numbers)
    assert all(len(group) == 5 for group in groups)
assert body.count('\\u200c') == body.count('بی\\u200cبی') == 1
print('Verified original Roman wording and three matching four-verse stanzas.')
PY

item.text:
Reconstructed all 12 verses in Urdu script and preserved the Roman wording in `romanLyrics`, with casing and verse-end punctuation normalized. Verified that both versions have three matching four-verse stanzas. Updated the titles and right-to-left direction, and removed `noUrdu`.

I read “Hussaina” as حسینا, “Allam” as عَلَم (standard), and “wo suna” as وہ سنا.
